written.myAnswer: Xylem transports water and mineral salts mainly upwards from the roots, while phloem transports food between sources and sinks and can carry it in either direction.

At the source, companion cells use energy to actively load sucrose into sieve tubes. Water enters from the xylem by osmosis, creating high pressure. The phloem sap flows towards the sink, where sucrose is unloaded. Water then moves back into the xylem by osmosis, lowering the pressure. This pressure difference drives bulk flow from source to sink.
